hens_rule_text: 1 hen per 800 sq ft of lot area, capped at 6 hens total per lot.
permit_notes: Secondary sources say no permit is required, but this was not confirmed on an official Providence city page and could not be verified in the zoning ordinance PDF directly.
setback_notes: Coop must be at least 20 ft from any dwelling, and the fenced enclosure at least 20 ft from any property line, per secondary summaries of the zoning ordinance's urban-agriculture provisions.
coop_rules: Coop must be covered/predator-proof, well ventilated, provide at least 2 sq ft per chicken, and be kept clean, dry and sanitary.
zoning_notes: Rules sit in the Providence Zoning Ordinance (Chapter 2014-39, No. 513) under its urban-agriculture provisions, which define terms like chicken coop; the ordinance has been amended multiple times through 2026 and the current PDF could not be downloaded from this machine to confirm the exact section number.
hoa_note: Homeowners associations, deed restrictions and leases can be stricter than city law. Check yours before getting chickens.

sources.name: Providence Rhode Island Chicken Ordinance, BackYard Chickens
City of Providence Zoning Ordinance (official PDF listing page)

research_notes: Attempts to download the current official zoning ordinance PDF from providenceri.gov failed (404 on two dated URLs, connection reset on a third), so the 1-hen-per-800-sq-ft rule, 6-hen cap, no-permit claim and 20 ft setback all come from secondary chicken-law aggregator sites rather than a direct read of the ordinance text; the exact code section number could not be confirmed and is left blank.
